title: Chapter 48: Please Let Me Go!
html:
He pictured Zhang Peng’s expression on the surveillance feed and felt a sudden sense of foreboding.Two nightmares about to meet each other.

The scraping did not stop when Zhang Peng entered. If the mirror entity had noticed him, it gave no sign.

I need to know what happens, but I am not going in there alone. The police are already on their way.

Chen Ge switched camera views, grabbed his phone and keys, and moved to a safer position from which he could monitor the scenario entrance.

For once, I am going to try not to be the most reckless person in this building.

He kept the dolls with him and waited, listening for movement from the sealed scenario.

…

Inside Murder by Midnight, Zhang Peng’s confidence was already beginning to fray. He had come to the park consumed by anger, but the dark, unfamiliar building did not behave the way he expected.

He had assumed the owner would be asleep in the staff room. Finding it empty had only sharpened his frustration.

In his agitation, Zhang Peng had injured himself while searching the room. The pain did nothing to improve his judgment.

Instead of leaving, he let resentment push him deeper into the Haunted House.

He ruined Ping An Apartments and sent Juan Er to prison. I am not leaving until I find him.

The scraping noise from above gave his anger a direction.

Zhang Peng followed the sound through the darkened corridors, moving carefully enough to avoid tripping over the scenery.

Close. It is coming from this floor.

He peered around the stairwell and entered the third-floor corridor, keeping close to the wall.

This place is a maze. How does anyone work in here without getting lost?

His mouth tightened into a humorless line.

The sound is just ahead. What is he doing up here this late?

Zhang Peng continued forward, following the scraping.

At the end of the third-floor corridor, near the scenario entrance, he saw a blurred black figure standing by the door. Something in its hand moved slowly across the wood.

Why is he standing in the dark?

Only when Zhang Peng drew closer did the wrongness of the silhouette register. Before he could reconsider, anger overrode caution and he rushed toward it.

“Found you!”

He collided with the shadow—or rather, passed straight through it and crashed into the door behind.

The triumphant expression on his face vanished instantly.

The impact sent him sprawling, stunned more by what had happened than by the fall.

“What was that?” Zhang Peng scrambled upright and spun around. “Where did he go?”

As his anger receded, something colder took its place.

I saw someone standing here. I know I did.

Abandoning any attempt at stealth, Zhang Peng used his phone for light. Scratch marks covered the door, and broken mirror fragments glittered on the floor.

Those marks were already here. So the shadow was real.

Then where did it go?

A shiver ran through him. The corridor suddenly looked far darker than it had a moment before.

People do not vanish into thin air… unless that was not a person.

He swallowed hard. The weak phone light no longer made him feel safer; it merely emphasized how much of the corridor remained unseen.

This place really is haunted.

Cold sweat spread across Zhang Peng’s forehead. Whatever revenge he had imagined no longer seemed important. He turned and hurried toward the stairs, thinking only of getting out.

In his panic, he failed to notice that the stairwell door was no longer positioned as he had left it.

I can think about everything else after I get outside.

He pushed into the stairwell—and recoiled when someone stepped from behind the door.

The sudden confrontation sent Zhang Peng stumbling backward, clutching his already injured arm.

“Stop.” Chen Ge emerged from the shadows in the Doctor Skull-Cracker costume, the distorted mask making the single word far more frightening than he intended.

His voice was unnervingly calm. Zhang Peng stared at him as though the Haunted House itself had come to life.Anyone. Someone. Please let there be a normal exit from this place.

Zhang Peng looked from Chen Ge to the enormous theatrical prop in his hands and decided that resistance was a poor idea.Why does the owner of a Haunted House look more terrifying than the ghost?

“The police are already outside,” Chen Ge said. “Do not make this worse.” He kept his distance and blocked the easiest route deeper into the attraction.

Bang!

A piece of scenery shifted as Zhang Peng lurched away. He abandoned what he had been carrying and bolted down the stairs.

“You broke into a Haunted House and this is where your courage gives out?”

Chen Ge followed, keeping him in sight while calling Inspector Lee rather than trying to tackle him in the dark.
